replacement: “Tut—tut—tut—sanctimonious talk and stock phrases! Old phrases and old gestures. The same old lies and ceremonial kowtowing. We know all about it. A kiss on the lips and a dagger in the heart, like in Schiller’s _Robbers_. I don’t like falsehood, Fathers. I want the truth. But the truth isn’t found in eating gudgeon, and I say so out loud! Father monks, why do you fast? Why do you expect a reward in heaven for it? For a reward like that, I’ll come and fast myself! No, saintly monk, you try being virtuous out in the world. Do some good for society, without locking yourself in a monastery at other people’s expense and without hoping for a reward up above—you’ll find that a bit harder. I can talk sense too, Father Superior. What have they got here?” He went up to the table. “Old port wine, and mead brewed by the Eliseyev Brothers. Fie, fie, Fathers! That’s a long way past gudgeon. Look at the bottles the fathers have set out, he he he! And who paid for all this? The Russian peasant, the working man, brings the farthing he earned with his horny hand, wrung from his family and the tax collector! You bleed the people, you know, holy fathers.”
